lessons.title: Kotlin's Built-in Result<T>
lessons.content: Kotlin's stdlib Result<T> wraps either a success value or a Throwable, letting you avoid try/catch at every call site while still being explicit about failure. runCatching { } builds one; getOrElse, getOrDefault, fold, onSuccess, and onFailure consume one functionally. Real scenario: a repository function that shouldn't crash the caller on a network failure but also shouldn't force every caller to write try/catch.

lessons.title: When to use Result<T> vs a Custom Sealed Result
lessons.content: Kotlin's Result<T> is great for simple success/failure with a Throwable, but it loses type information about WHAT went wrong beyond the exception type. For domain layers where callers need to react differently to different failure categories (validation vs network vs auth), a custom sealed class (as covered in the Sealed Classes chapter) gives compiler-enforced exhaustive handling that Result<T> can't. Rule of thumb: Result<T> for simple utility/infra code, sealed hierarchies for domain-level business logic with distinct error categories.
